title: Caramelized Onion and Cottage Cheese Dip
description: Slowly browned onion is blended with no-salt-added cottage cheese for a smooth, savory dip with a little sweetness.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

steps.title: Caramelize the onion
steps.text: Warm {oil} in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Add {onion} and cook for 22–30 minutes, stirring often until fully caramelized, soft and golden brown. Use a little {broth} whenever the pan starts to catch.

steps.title: Capture the pan flavor
steps.text: Pour in the remaining broth, scrape the pan and simmer for 1 minute. Transfer the onions and liquid to a shallow dish and refrigerate until cold.

steps.title: Whip the dip
steps.text: Blend the cooled onion mixture with {cheese} and {chives} for 45–60 seconds, scraping down the jug, until no curds or onion strands remain.

steps.title: Adjust the consistency
steps.text: Scrape all of the mixture into the measuring cup. Add cold water a teaspoon at a time if needed to reach about 1 1/2 cups, maintaining a smooth spoonable texture.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chill for 30 minutes. Serve with tender potatoes, or spoon over warm chicken and its gravy.

notes: Yield: About 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Caramelize the onion the day before and refrigerate it. Blend the dip on the day you serve it. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Cottage cheese releases whey after freezing, which affects this whipped texture. Fridge reheat: Serve chilled. Stir until smooth just before portioning. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw covered in the refrigerator, then whisk or blend briefly and serve cold. For dairy-free dip, use the same volume of plain blended silken tofu and keep the caramelized onions and chives. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 53 kcal, 5.6 g protein, 3.4 g total carbohydrate, 2.1 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 17 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
